title: The Queen Cancer Stem Cell Hypothesis: A Unified Theory of Primary, Secondary, and Unknown-Origin Cancers Based on Seven Principles
content: Cancer is currently classified by anatomical site, histology, immunohistochemistry, for the distinction between primary and metastatic lesions. This classification does not explain why a primary tumor continues to grow after the cell that initiated it has left, why a migrating cancer stem cell can create a new primary tumor in a distant organ, why the liver can simultaneously host a metastasis from a primary colon cancer and a second primary liver cancer, or why some secondary cancers exist without a detectable primary. This paper proposes a novel insight, the Queen Cancer Stem Cell Hypothesis based on seven principles. The central claim of the hypothesis is that no primary cancer arises in any organ without a cancer stem cell, that this the Queen cell which initiates, promotes and propagates the primary malignant tumor in that organ, then the queen cancer stem cell leaves the first primary cancer of the organ of origin, migrates through blood, lymphatics, and interstitial fluid, maintains signaling control over its direct offspring only (the first primary is the direct offspring) , and at the same time, this circulating stem cell retains the ability to create new primary cancers in any distant organ as a migrating cell. So, Metastases are controlled by the primary tumor cells, not by the migrating Queen cell. A secondary cancer of unknown origin can be a true primary created by a migrating Queen cell. This framework redefines metastasis to metastasis spread, primary versus secondary classification, and cancer of unknown primary as phenomena of lineage, kinship, and signaling, not anatomy alone.
